chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Khattab, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from one who narrated to him, from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-'Ala', Abu al-Ma'za, and 'Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat, their group, from Abi Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no martyr except that he wishes, if al-Husayn ibn Ali were alive, and he wishes to be with al-Husayn (peace be upon him) so that they may enter Paradise with him.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ بْنُ عَلِيٍّ: al-Husayn ibn Ali (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: Why do all martyrs wish to be with Imam Husayn in Paradise?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elucidates the unique spiritual hierarchy of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) by stating that every martyr yearns to be in his company and enter Paradise with him. This hadith underscores the concept of 'Shahid al-Husayn' not merely as a title for his companions, but as a universal aspiration for all martyrs, affirming his preeminent status among the Ahl al-Bayt and the broader community of believers.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from his uncle Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from someone who narrated to him, from ‘Ali ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Ḥusain ibn Abil ‘Alā, Abil Maghrā, and ‘Āsim ibn Ḥumayd Al-Ḥannāť, from Abī Basīr, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
All of the martyrs wish to be with Ḥusain (a.s.) so that they can enter Paradise with him.
